lever: read through the premature TGA to make full-length protein
verdict: DEGRADED - and the lead compound has no verified product
reason: The stop codon TGA is the most permissive, but the +4 base read from the reference is A - the LEAST permissive position in the C>U>G>A hierarchy - so the context works against readthrough. Near-cognate decoding would insert Trp, Arg or Cys, not Leu. The transcript is also NMD-competent, so there is little message left to read through, and no NMD inhibitor is approved. The obvious approved readthrough route, aminoglycosides, is excluded by nephrocalcinosis. UPDATE: openFDA returns a single record for ataluren and it is BULK INGREDIENT - no NDA and no ANDA, so there is no approved product in the United States, and the EU conditional authorisation was reportedly not renewed in March 2025. The axis may therefore fail this project's own rule that only medicines already in human use qualify; the candidate is retained with an explicit flag and zero executability pending an EMA check rather than deleted on an assumption.

lever: raise the amount of the destabilised missense protein that survives quality control
verdict: OPEN - best mechanistic fit, and now with an approved product
reason: If allele 2 is cleared by chaperone-dependent quality control, chaperone capacity is the matching lever and the only one that acts on the causal lesion. Counter-argument that keeps it off the nomination list: enhancing proteostasis is an antidote to aneuploidy-selective vulnerability, so it may also protect pre-malignant aneuploid cells in a child who already has a sarcoma. UPDATE: arimoclomol, a heat-shock response co-inducer, was approved by the FDA in September 2024 (MIPLYFFA, NDA, in combination with miglustat, adult and paediatric patients 2 years and older) - confirmed against openFDA, which returns the NDA directly while the target database still records PHASE_3. This axis therefore now has an approved medicine behind it and holds the top rank, which it did not when the axis was first written. The counter-argument is unchanged.

lever: block the deacetylation that routes BubR1 to degradation
reason: Mechanistically the most on-target 'up' lever available, and absent from this project's first pass by construction: the node set was defined STRUCTURALLY - what the machine is built of - not REGULATORILY, so nothing that merely sets the level of a component could enter it. Three reasons it still fails here. (1) Pathway mismatch: a destabilised missense allele is cleared by chaperone-dependent quality control, not by the K668 acetylation route, so the lever and the lesion sit on different pathways for THIS allele class. (2) The lifespan result was obtained with transgenic SIRT2 overexpression, not with a drug. (3) Tumours are NAD+-avid, which is the entire rationale for NAMPT inhibitors, and this child has an active sarcoma.

Rejected on the pathway that is already broken. TORC1 inactivation promotes APC/C-dependent mitotic slippage (PMID:35141499), and the specific lesion here is a weakened MCC inhibitory signal toward APC/C-CDC20. A drug that promotes APC/C-dependent slippage pushes the same lever the disease already pushes. Any muscle or growth benefit would be bought by worsening the primary defect.

lever: remove cells that have accumulated damage
reason: Growth suppression, delayed epiphyseal closure and osteopenia are recorded paediatric harms of the tyrosine-kinase-inhibitor senolytic, and growth failure with short stature is this child's presenting complaint - the drug's main harm and the patient's main problem are the same axis. Senescence may also act as a tumour-suppressive barrier in embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma. Requires label-level confirmation, which a target database cannot provide.

lever: remove the buffer that lets aneuploid cells cope
reason: Kept as tumour-only rather than vetoed outright, but the branch rests on a tumour-versus-tissue selective window that has NOT been demonstrated. Somatic tissue appears to need autophagy to tolerate aneuploidy, so if no selective window exists the correct verdict is a veto in both contexts rather than a split. Stated here as an open decision point, not a settled call.

lever: exploit the higher metabolic and proteotoxic load aneuploid cells carry
reason: Retained in the candidate list on request after an earlier pass moved it to contraindications. The chromosomal-instability literature behind it is weak but real. Two objections stand and retaining it does not resolve them: a black box warning against chronic paediatric exposure, and antiproliferative pressure in a child whose presenting complaint is growth failure. The direction-of-effect tension is unresolved, because the metabolic stress argued to harm tumour cells also acts on somatic tissue.

lever: restore the kinase-phosphatase balance tipped by reduced PP2A-B56 recruitment
reason: The only node where available chemistry acts in the corrective direction somatically, and the aim would be PARTIAL rebalancing with a defined ceiling, since over-correction arrests cells in mitosis. Not one of the compounds is approved.

No validated small molecule restores a weakened checkpoint. Compounds described as checkpoint activators act by perturbing mitosis, and the MPS1/TTK pipeline is entirely inhibitory. This is the structural result: the checkpoint is built of stoichiometric complex components, the mechanism needs more function, and small-molecule pharmacology delivers less.

lever: treat the features the child actually presents with
verdict: OPEN - the only arm with approved medicines
reason: The one place where approved medicines meet this child's phenotype, and therefore the only arm with a near-term path. Matching is recorded per row as registered-indication versus mechanism-only, because the two are not the same evidence.

Renal ultrasound and a cancer-predisposition protocol. Wilms tumour is documented in PCS/MVA and biallelic TRIP13; a reported MVA3 case had a Wilms tumour at age 3 and an orbital rhabdomyosarcoma nine years later. The most valuable Track 2 output here is not a medicine.

lever: find out whether BUBR1 abundance is actually reduced
reason: A BUBR1 western blot on the child's cells and a premature-chromatid-separation rate by G-banding with centromere FISH. If BUBR1 abundance is normal, the premise under every abundance-raising axis above fails, and that would be reported.

lever: stop aneuploid cells contributing to tissue
direction_needed: none - wrong direction in somatic tissue
reason: The organism already does this and it IS the phenotype: aneuploid cells carry proteotoxic stress from stoichiometric imbalance, activate p53 and proliferate poorly, so growth failure and reduced birth size are in large part the consequence of aneuploid cells failing to divide. Pushing harder deepens the growth deficit. There is also no selectivity handle - the distinguishing features are quantitative and shared with any stressed proliferating cell. In a NEWBORN the argument inverts hardest: nephrogenesis completes around 34-36 weeks of gestation and never resumes, so arrest in that window removes nephrons permanently, which is the worst possible price against a renal phenotype. Finally, because every cell carries the germline hypomorph, arresting the currently-aneuploid fraction selects for euploid cells that will regenerate the problem: this is a FLUX problem, not a stock problem.

lever: convert aneuploid cells into a stable non-dividing state
direction_needed: decrease - tumour only, and only paired with clearance
reason: The decisive experiment was done in this exact genetic background and points the other way: hypomorphic BubR1 mice are a progeroid model whose phenotype is driven by accumulating p16-positive senescent cells, and CLEARING those cells delayed ageing-associated disorders (PMID:22048312 - healthspan improved, survival 'not substantially extended', and the lifespan figures usually quoted alongside it come from wild-type animals). Senescence is also worse than plain arrest here, for three reasons: the cell persists and is apoptosis-resistant, so in tissue still being built it blocks a niche instead of vacating it; the secretory programme acts paracrinally, and a chronic inflammatory field is tumour-promoting in a child who already has a cancer predisposition; and the flux objection is untouched, since euploid cells carrying the hypomorph keep producing new aneuploid ones, so an ongoing stream becomes an accumulating pool. The cell-autonomous tumour-suppressive effect is real and senescence is a recognised barrier in embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma - which is why the axis stays OPEN for the tumour, but only as induction FOLLOWED BY senolytic clearance. Induction without clearance leaves precisely the secretory cells this disease cannot afford.

layer: the APC/C step itself - substitution rather than restoration
lever: supply from outside the restraint on APC/C that the weakened MCC fails to produce
direction_needed: decrease - one of three nodes needing down, and the only one where the lesion IS the missing restraint
verdict: CLOSED - no chemical matter, and aimed at the wrong defect
reason: Logically the best-posed idea in the whole project, and the only one that inverts this report's central obstacle. Three nodes require the direction to be down somatically - AURKB and BIRC5, because Aurora B is relatively unopposed once KARD-mediated PP2A-B56 recruitment falls, and APC/C-CDC20, because it is prematurely active. APC/C is not the only one, but it is the only one where the lesion ITSELF is the missing restraint, so inhibiting it substitutes for the defective function rather than rebalancing a downstream consequence. The signed network already records CDC20 required_normal = decrease. It is also substitution rather than restoration: it does not repair BubR1, it replaces the restraint BubR1 can no longer impose. | CHEMISTRY: absent. All seven APC/C subunits and coactivators in the node set return zero compounds and zero approved (ANAPC1, ANAPC16, CDC20, CDC23, CDC26, CDC27, FZR1). The known inhibitors - proTAME, which blocks coactivator IR-tail binding, and apcin, which occupies the D-box receptor of Cdc20 - are research tools with no clinical development, so they fail this project's requirement of medicines already in human use. | CONCEPTUAL TRAP: inhibiting CDC20 is NOT the same intervention as inhibiting APC/C. Cdc20 is simultaneously the APC/C coactivator and a subunit of the MCC, so a Cdc20-directed drug also weakens the complex whose action one is trying to reinforce. The two must never be conflated. | OBJECTIONS: (1) a drug is an unconditional brake whereas the checkpoint is a conditional one - the SAC restrains APC/C only until attachments are correct and then releases, while a small molecule restrains constantly in every dividing cell, arresting proliferating tissue in a child whose presenting complaint is growth failure. (2) Prolonged mitotic arrest resolves into either death or slippage, so the intervention can produce the outcome it was meant to prevent - and where cyclin B already leaks fast, slippage is the likelier branch. (3) It is adjacent to a class already contraindicated here: taxanes and vinca alkaloids also end with APC/C restrained and cells held in mitosis. The distinction is real, since an APC/C inhibitor does not damage the spindle and therefore does not CREATE new missegregation, but the shared end state carries most of the same objection. (4) DECISIVE: it targets the wrong defect. APC/C inhibition addresses premature anaphase ONSET, a timing defect, whereas the cytogenetic hallmark of this disease is premature chromatid SEPARATION - sisters already parted before anaphase, seen in metaphase spreads without a primary constriction. If cohesion protection has failed, holding securin undegraded does not restore pairing, because separase was never the proximate cause. | WHAT SURVIVES: partial rather than complete restraint, on the same defined-ceiling logic applied to Aurora B - lengthen the arrest just enough to permit error correction without blocking exit. Coherent as a hypothesis, but it needs dose control no approved drug offers and a biomarker that does not exist. The conceptually correct target is narrower still: strengthen the specific weakened interaction by raising BubR1 occupancy of the Cdc20 degron pockets. That is a protein-protein interaction STABILISER - a molecular-glue problem, not an inhibitor - and no such compound exists. Worth naming because it shows the gap is one of MODALITY, not of target.

axis: delay separase activation - the cutting step itself
layer: the protease that physically separates the chromatids
lever: prolong either restraint on separase (securin binding, or cyclin B1-CDK1 binding) so that cohesin is cut later
direction_needed: decrease separase activity - the step closest to the cytogenetic readout
verdict: CLOSED - no chemical matter, and the one druggable target fails on direction
reason: Better posed than restraining APC/C, because premature chromatid separation is the cytogenetic hallmark and this axis acts one step closer to that readout. Separase is held back two independent ways: securin binds and inhibits it, and cyclin B1-CDK1 binding inhibits it separately; prolonging either would postpone cutting. Censused 12 targets against release 26.09 (data/separase_axis_census.tsv): ESPL1 (separase itself), PTTG1 (securin), CCNB1, SGO1, SGO2, PPP2R5A, PPP2R5B, CDCA5 (sororin), WAPL, RAD21 and STAG2 return ZERO compounds of any kind - 11 of 12. The sole exception is CDK1 with 12 compounds, none approved and every one an INHIBITOR, which is the wrong direction twice over: cyclin B1-CDK1 inhibits separase, so inhibiting CDK1 releases it and would accelerate the exact step this axis exists to postpone. Both surviving restraints are protein-protein interactions, so the required modality is a STABILISER or molecular glue. STABILISER is a recognised direction in config/action_type_effects.tsv and not one compound in the entire census carries it. Same conclusion as direct APC/C inhibition, reached from the opposite end of the pathway: the gap is one of modality, not of target.
